title: QualGuard: Explainable Embedding Change Investigator & Offline Quality Harness
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Model/config rollouts for embedding + reranker changes are triggering noisy alerts and ambiguous regression signals today. We need a reproducible, explainable offline investigation path that ties config/model diffs to concrete recall/precision shifts and ranking deltas across representative cohorts.

Goal: Deliver 'QualGuard' — an automated offline investigator and quality harness that (1) computes cohort-level recall/precision and ranking concordance between baseline and candidate embeddings/rerankers, (2) produces explainability artifacts (per-query feature deltas, token-level perturbation sensitivity, nearest-neighbor drift heatmaps), and (3) surfaces actionable triage suggestions (accept, revert, restrict rollout, require targeted evals).

Scope: Offline-only harness initially (no realtime gate). Focus on embedding + reranker pairs used in search and suggestions product areas. Support config diffs including quantization level, candidate model, batching profile, and embedding normalization changes. Provide dashboards and a lightweight investigator CLI.

Out of scope: Online rollback automation, full A/B experimentation integration, UI polish beyond raw dashboards and links.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can re-run a saved production query cohort against baseline and candidate embedding+reranker configurations and emit recall@K (K=1,5,10) and normalized MRR deltas
Explainability artifacts generated per cohort: top-100 nearest-neighbor shift list, per-query token-perturbation sensitivity score, and a ranked list of queries driving the largest quality change
Automated triage recommendation produced with confidence band (accept / soft-block / hard-block) and a short rationale string
Investigation run artifacts stored in S3 and linked in the CI job output; run completes for 10k queries within 45 minutes on the staging infra profile
Unit and integration tests cover scoring logic, dataset loaders, and drift metric computation; example CLI run and sample dashboard produced
Documentation for engineers and PMs describing interpretation and recommended follow-ups
steps: Design scoring surface: define recall/precision/MRR variants, ranking concordance (Kendall/Tau), and per-query sensitivity metrics
Instrument dataset loader to pull saved production cohorts with metadata tags (traffic segment, timeframe, user cohort)
Implement offline runner that loads two embedding+reranker configs, computes dense NN retrieval, reranks, and computes delta metrics
Add explainability module producing nearest-neighbor shift CSVs, example hard-negative reconstructions, and token-level perturbation traces
Wire runner output to S3 with deterministic run IDs and minimal schema for downstream dashboards
Add CI job and sample dataset; validate runtime SLA on staging; produce dashboard snapshot
Gather design review feedback and iterate on triage threshold defaults

2025-03-11 - Diego Alvarez: Initial design sketched. We'll reuse the offline retrieval pipeline from ENG-43021 and add an explainability layer. Blocking question: storage format for NN shift snapshots (Parquet vs CSV).
2025-03-12 - Priya Nair (PM): Prioritize triage recommendation output — PMs need a simple signal for canary hold. Suggested 'soft-block' to mean require shadow evaluation in prod-like load.

2025-03-13 - Diego Alvarez: Implemented baseline vs candidate runner + recall/MRR computation (draft). Working on nearest-neighbor delta exporter. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/emb-quality-harness/pull/72
2025-03-14 - Security (J. Park): Confirmed no customer PII will be exported; ensure masking of user IDs in artifacts. Added a checklist item to docs.

2025-03-16 - Design review (L. O'Neill): Reviewed explainability artifacts; requested clearer visualization of query clusters that drive regression and a small integration test covering a simulated cohort with injected drift

2025-03-18 - Diego Alvarez: Runner performance optimized by incremental ANN cache; end-to-end run time for 10k queries in staging measured at 38 minutes. Next: hook up triage thresholds and add dashboard links in CI output.
